input_signals.name: Profit Net of Debt Service Burden
input_signals.expression: SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating profitability is only free cash for shareholders after interest and near-term debt maturities are covered; the same EBITDA yield is worth far less when a large fraction of it is pre-committed to servicing and rolling debt.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the ROE−ROA wedge entirely, so there is no division by book equity and no sign flip for loss-makers or firms with negative or near-zero equity; all quantities are asset-scaled and strictly comparable. It is also not the additive twin of a leverage sort because only the serviceable portion of debt enters — interest actually paid plus debt actually maturing — so long-dated, cheaply financed leverage is treated as benign while short-dated, expensive leverage directly consumes profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) )

input_signals.name: Retained Earnings Corroborated Profit
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at)), RANK(RATIO(re, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Current operating profitability is credible only when the firm has actually accumulated earnings over its life; high current margins with little retained earnings signal a transient or first-cycle profit, while deep retained earnings without current profitability signal decay.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN of two ranks is a strict conjunction, not an additive composite: a firm scores high only if it clears both the current-profit and the cumulative-profit-history bar, so the long leg is exactly "durable operating strength" and neither single-theme sort reproduces it. Retained earnings to assets is a long-horizon persistence proxy that requires no rolling window, so unlike five-year volatility measures it costs no coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), at ) ), rank( ratio( re, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Trough Profit Versus Fixed Claims
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(SUB(TS_MIN(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: The relevant test of durable operating strength is whether the firm's worst recent year of profitability would still have covered its committed interest and maturing debt; firms passing this stress test have profits that cannot be extinguished by a normal downturn.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the current profit level with its five-year minimum turns the financing adjustment into an explicit downside stress test, so the signal separates firms whose current coverage rests on a cyclical peak from those whose floor clears their claims — a state-dependent mechanism no accruals or cash-profitability measure captures. Both terms remain asset-scaled and unit-consistent, and the trough operator is the sharpest available expression of "persistent" in the economic story.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( sub( ts_min( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: Persistent Claim Coverage Count
input_signals.expression: TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(oibdp, ADD(xint, dlc)), 0), 5)
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters is how reliably, not how amply, operating profit has covered committed interest and maturing debt; a firm that cleared its fixed claims in every one of the last five years has demonstrated persistence that a single high coverage reading cannot.
input_signals.reasoning: Used alone the 0-5 count avoids the scale-mismatch problem that sank the earlier count-weighted rank product, and it converts the archive's best-performing comparison into a pure frequency-of-solvency measure, which is a different statistic from either the current spread or its five-year minimum. Comparing it against the trough version tells us whether the payoff comes from persistence of coverage or from the depth of the worst year.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ts_sum( indicator( sub( oibdp, add( xint, dlc ) ), 0 ), 5 )

input_signals.name: Standardized Profit Less Rollover Risk
input_signals.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A given operating margin is worth less when a large share of near-term debt must be refinanced from a thin stock of liquid assets, because funding-market shocks force distressed asset sales or dilution exactly when the profit stream should be capitalized.
input_signals.reasoning: The critique was purely about commensurability, and standardizing each winsorized leg to unit cross-sectional dispersion means the rollover-pressure term can no longer swamp the profitability term, so the sort reflects a true trade-off rather than a rescaled liquidity ratio. The mechanism remains distinct from the archive's interest-cost channel because it prices debt *maturity and liquidity backing* rather than the price of debt.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Standardized Profit Earnings History Floor
input_signals.expression: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(re, at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength requires both a high current operating margin and a genuinely accumulated stock of past earnings, and the binding constraint is whichever dimension is weaker on a comparable scale.
input_signals.reasoning: Standardizing both legs to unit dispersion before the MIN is the precise fix for the critic's objection: neither retained-earnings-to-assets nor the operating margin can dominate the minimum by scale alone, so the conjunction binds on either side across the cross-section and the signal cannot collapse into the retained-earnings anomaly. Unlike the gen-1 rank version, ZSCORE preserves the extreme tails that the long-short spread needs, which is why that version had a 2.07 FMB t-stat but no alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( re, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Uncommitted Profit Less Levered Erosion
input_signals.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is high current profit relative to committed claims *and* the absence of margin erosion from the firm's own demonstrated peak; the two conditions identify different firms, so a long-short built on both should be stronger than either alone.
input_signals.reasoning: This unites the archive's best long-side channel (profit net of interest and maturing debt, alpha 2.8-3.2%) with its best short-side channel (levered margin erosion, alpha −6.6%) after standardizing each so that the skewed erosion term cannot dominate variance — the precise fix for its flat FMB slope. If both fmb_tstat and ls_talpha exceed the leader, the lesson is that the family's payoff has two economically separate sources and should be built two-sided from here on.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( mul( sub( ts_max( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ), ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Health Weighted Profitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The profitability premium is concentrated among financially healthy firms: a strong operating margin is a claim on future cash flows only if near-term refinancing needs cannot force the firm to liquidate assets first, so profitability should be weighted by refinancing safety rather than merely added to it.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has only tested additive and standardized-difference combinations of profitability and financial health; this is a genuine conditional in which the health rank acts as a bounded [0,1] weight on the standardized profit z-score, so profitability differences matter most where the balance sheet permits them to be harvested. Using RANK for the weight and ZSCORE for the profit level avoids the sign pathology of multiplying two signed z-scores, in which two negatives would spuriously score high.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Industry Relative Profit Less Rollover Risk
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Both attainable margins and normal short-term funding structures are set largely by industry technology and inventory cycles, so only within-industry deviations in profitability and in refinancing pressure identify firm-specific durable strength.
input_signals.reasoning: This varies exactly one preprocessing choice on the current archive leader, and the diagnostic value is high: if industry demeaning raises ls_talpha and Sharpe, the leader's spread was partly a static sector bet (asset-light versus inventory-heavy industries) and every subsequent construct should be industry-standardized, whereas if it degrades the result the cross-industry component is genuine risk-pricing information worth keeping. It is a targeted design test on the best-performing mechanism rather than a new mechanism, which is why only one slot is spent on it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Refinancing pressure and margin erosion are economically distinct fragility routes — one is a funding-market risk, the other a franchise-decay risk — so subtracting both from operating profitability should identify durable strength more sharply than removing either alone.
input_signals.reasoning: The two penalty channels are the archive's best-performing quality legs and are unlikely to be redundant (a cash-rich firm with a decaying franchise has no rollover risk, and an inventory-heavy grower at its own margin peak has no erosion), so their combination tests whether the leader's alpha and the erosion signal's alpha are additive. All three legs are winsorized and standardized to unit dispersion, so no term can dominate the sort by scale, which is what made the earlier unstandardized versions degenerate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( mul( sub( ts_max( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ), ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Erosion Weighted Profitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Current profitability deserves credit only from firms that have not been losing margin against fixed obligations; the franchise-decay state should scale the profitability premium rather than be netted against it.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the targeted repair of the archive's largest-alpha but zero-slope signal: mapping levered erosion into a bounded [0,1] rank weight removes its extreme skew (the cause of the flat FMB slope) while preserving its portfolio-relevant ordering, and the same weighting structure already delivered 3.5% alpha with a 2.34 FMB t-stat when applied to rollover risk. If it beats both parents, conditional weighting rather than standardized differencing becomes the preferred structure for the remaining generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( winsor( mul( sub( ts_max( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ), ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Less Maturity Concentration
input_signals.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes near-term debt dangerous for a profitable firm is the concentration of claims falling due relative to all claims — a maturity-structure choice — rather than merely the thinness of liquid assets available to repay it.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a one-input anatomy test of the current leader that distinguishes two economically different readings of dlc/act: liquidity backing versus maturity concentration; because lt is the denominator the leg is scale-free, defined for nearly all firms, and orthogonal to inventory-cycle differences that drive act. The result tells us whether future refinements should push toward liquidity measures or toward debt-structure measures, which is a decision the archive cannot currently make.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Industry Profit Less Absolute Rollover Risk
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Attainable margins are technology- and industry-determined, so profitability should be judged against industry peers, whereas refinancing pressure is priced by capital markets on an absolute basis and its cross-industry variation is genuine risk information rather than a nuisance sector tilt.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-3 pair showed that demeaning both legs raised the FMB slope (2.90→3.27) but cut alpha (3.5%→2.8%) and Sharpe (0.30→0.19), which implies the informative demeaning is on the profitability leg while the fragility leg's absolute level carries the abnormal return. This asymmetric standardization is the direct implication of that evidence and should, if the diagnosis is right, dominate both parents on slope and alpha simultaneously.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Conversion Weighted Coverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profit that exceeds committed claims is only credible if it arrives as cash: accrual-inflated earnings cannot service interest or repay maturing debt, so the coverage spread should be weighted by the degree to which reported income is cash-backed.
input_signals.reasoning: This opens the earnings-quality channel that the archive has never tested, but does so as a bounded conditioner on the solvency-adjusted profit spread rather than as an additive accruals leg, so it cannot collapse into the Sloan sort — a firm with pristine cash conversion but no coverage still scores near zero. The mechanism is a genuine interaction: cash conversion matters precisely because the claims are contractual and must be paid in cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Supplier Financed Profit Discount
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), act), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating profitability that rests on heavy non-debt operating liabilities — stretched payables and accrued expenses funding the working-capital cycle — is lower quality than the same margin earned with self-funded working capital, because operating-liability leverage inflates returns on invested capital while creating claims that tighten precisely when trade creditors reassess the firm.
input_signals.reasoning: This drops the smoothing-knob idea and instead opens a quality channel the archive has never touched: fragility from *operating* liabilities rather than from financial debt, maturity structure, franchise erosion, or accruals, so it is informative regardless of outcome and should be largely orthogonal to the dlc-based legs already tested. It uses the bounded-rank conditioning structure that has produced the archive's best joint results (Health Weighted Profitability: alpha 3.5%, Sharpe 0.28), and all inputs are broadly reported so coverage should hold at the archive norm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), act ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Industry Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is a within-industry margin advantage that is not offset by absolute refinancing pressure and not undermined by franchise decay against fixed obligations; the three conditions are economically separate and their evidence should compound.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's two best signals improved along orthogonal axes — industry demeaning of the profitability leg lifted the FMB slope from 2.90 to 3.80, and adding the erosion leg lifted alpha from 3.5% to 3.8% with t from 3.26 to 3.55 — so their union is the single highest-value untested point and directly targets joint strength rather than one metric. Every leg is winsorized and unit-standardized, so the composite cannot be captured by the leg with the fattest tail.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( mul( sub( ts_max( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ), ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Balance Sheet Accrual Weighted Coverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1), dp), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profit in excess of committed claims is credible only if it is not manufactured by working-capital accruals net of capital consumption, because contractual interest and maturing debt must be paid in cash rather than in receivables and inventory.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the specific failure of Cash Conversion Weighted Coverage, whose mechanism produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.44) and 3.7% alpha but whose oancf input cut coverage to 0.080; the balance-sheet accrual definition uses only act, lct and dp, which are reported throughout the sample, so the same economic conditioner should survive at roughly 0.12 coverage. If the statistics hold up with coverage restored, the earnings-quality conditioner becomes a permanent component; if they collapse, the earlier result was a sample-period artifact.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( sub( act, lct ), 1 ), dp ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Coverage Level Less Coverage Drawdown
input_signals.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(TS_MAX(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 5), SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters for durability is the firm's current cushion of profit over committed claims *and* how far that cushion has fallen from its own five-year peak, since a shrinking solvency cushion signals that obligations were sized against profits the firm no longer earns.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has applied the own-history drawdown operator to the raw margin and to leverage separately, but never to the solvency cushion itself, which is the quantity the economic story says must be stable; measuring level and drawdown of the same object also guarantees the two legs are economically commensurable rather than one being a repackaged leverage sort. This is the natural successor to Coverage Level Plus Improvement (alpha 3.3%, t 3.44), replacing a one-year change with a peak-relative deterioration state.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( sub( ts_max( sub( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ), 5 ), sub( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( add( xint, dlc ), at ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Solvency Gated Profitability Premium
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), INDICATOR(SUB(act, ADD(lct, dlc)), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: The profitability premium is a claim on future distributable cash and is only harvestable where the balance sheet cannot force intervention: among firms whose liquid assets exceed all current obligations including maturing debt, margin differences should predict returns, whereas among firms failing that test returns are dominated by distress dynamics and profitability carries little information.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike a rank product, this is not a monotone re-weighting that collapses toward an additive combination — it is a regime switch that sets the profitability bet to exactly zero for firms failing the liquidity test, so the long and short legs are both drawn from the solvent subsample and the signal makes no profitability bet at all inside the distressed regime. The gate is a genuine accounting inequality (act versus lct plus dlc) rather than a tuned threshold, and it directly tests the archive's central premise that profitability information is conditional on financial health rather than merely additive with it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), indicator( sub( act, add( lct, dlc ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Less Maturity Shortening
input_signals.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: When creditors shorten a firm's funding — the share of claims coming due within a year rises — they are signalling reduced confidence in the durability of its cash flows, so profitability accompanied by maturity shortening is transient while equally profitable firms that are terming out their obligations have creditor-certified durability.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the erosion-times-leverage family entirely and introduces a credit-supply mechanism: the *change* in maturity composition rather than any level of debt, erosion, or liquidity, which makes it largely orthogonal to CMA, to the static dlc legs already tested, and to the failed own-history leverage creep measure (a level-of-liabilities concept, not a composition concept). The static version of this channel is already productive (Profit Less Maturity Concentration: fmb 2.59, alpha 3.2%, coverage 0.144), so testing its first difference isolates whether creditors' revisions carry information beyond the standing structure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( delta( ratio( dlc, lt ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Less Volatile Demand Rollover Risk
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(VOL(GROWTH(sale, 1), 5), RATIO(dlc, act)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Refinancing needs are only dangerous for businesses whose revenues can fall sharply; a firm with volatile demand and near-term debt to roll faces funding withdrawal exactly when its sales dip, whereas a stable-revenue firm can carry the same maturing debt safely.
input_signals.reasoning: Every fragility leg tested so far has been purely balance-sheet; this introduces demand-side instability from the income statement and multiplies it with the archive's best fragility channel, so the penalty applies only where cash-flow risk and funding risk co-occur. It is distinct from the failed earnings-volatility × total-debt charge because the risk is measured on revenue (the exogenous driver) and paired with the *maturing* rather than total debt, which is the claim that actually forces a funding decision.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( mul( vol( growth( sale, 1 ), 5 ), ratio( dlc, act ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cumulative Earning Power Versus Claims
input_signals.expression: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oibdp, 5), lt), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The most reliable measure of durable operating strength is how many years of accumulated operating profit it would take to extinguish all creditor claims; five years of realized profit relative to total liabilities captures persistence and financial health jointly in a way a single-year margin cannot.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the profitability measure from a one-year asset-scaled margin to a multi-year cumulative flow benchmarked against the claim stock — a persistence concept the archive has only tested through fragile trend, count, and trough constructions, all of which failed for statistical rather than economic reasons. Pairing it with the proven rollover leg isolates whether cumulated earning power adds information beyond the current margin while keeping the winning architecture intact.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( zscore( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( oibdp, 5 ), lt ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit With History Position Less Rollover
input_signals.expression: SUB(ADD(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(TS_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm's margin is durable when it is both high relative to industry peers and standing near the top of its own recent history; position within own history captures the same franchise-health information as peak-relative erosion but without conflating it with the size of the fall.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the targeted statistical repair of the leader's weakest component: TS_RANK is bounded and near-uniform by construction, so it carries a real cross-sectional slope where the zero-inflated erosion product does not (standalone slope −0.15), while expressing the same "profit above its own recent norm" economics. If it matches the leader's alpha with a higher FMB slope and better coverage, the final consolidated signal should use own-history position rather than the skewed drawdown interaction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( add( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( ts_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Less Rollover Less Idiosyncratic Decay
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Margin declines that are shared with industry peers are cyclical and mean-reverting, whereas a firm losing margin while its peers hold theirs is losing pricing power or share permanently; only the idiosyncratic component of decay should be penalized alongside refinancing pressure.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a lookback-window change but a decomposition of decay into cyclical and firm-specific parts — the archive has never separated the two, and it is the economically correct way to distinguish transient from durable profitability deterioration. Because the leg is an industry-demeaned first difference it is roughly symmetric and free of the zero-inflation that flattened the erosion leg's cross-sectional slope, while requiring only two years of data so coverage should exceed the five-year leader's 0.117.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( neg( ind_adj( delta( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Less Rollover Less Supplier Days
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), cogs), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm that is stretching suppliers — carrying many days of payables and accruals relative to its cost of goods — depends on trade-creditor forbearance, a claim that can tighten independently of the debt market and that inflates measured returns on capital.
input_signals.reasoning: Scaling non-debt current liabilities by cost of goods rather than by current assets removes the algebraic complementarity the critic identified (dlc/act and (lct−dlc)/act summing to lct/act) and turns the leg into a genuine days-payable intensity measure driven by purchasing terms rather than by the same denominator as the rollover leg. The two fragility legs are then economically and statistically distinct: one measures debt coming due against liquid resources, the other measures how hard the firm is leaning on its supply chain.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), cogs ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Adjusted Profit Less Rollover
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Because R&D is expensed rather than capitalized, reported operating profit understates the true operating strength of research-intensive firms; adding research spending back gives a cleaner measure of the cash-generating capability that must be judged against refinancing needs.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a candidate improvement rather than an ablation: R&D-intensive firms are systematically penalized by the current profitability leg while also being the firms least able to support debt with tangible collateral, so correcting the measurement should sharpen both legs' economic alignment. COALESCE treats unreported R&D as genuine zero spending — the standard and economically justified convention — so coverage is unaffected, and the test tells us whether the leader's profitability leg is mismeasured for the intangible-intensive part of the cross-section.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Profit Less Rollover Less Idiosyncratic Decay
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is high investment-adjusted profitability relative to industry peers, unthreatened by near-term refinancing needs and not eroding faster than the industry cycle explains; the three conditions are economically distinct and should compound.
input_signals.reasoning: This unites the two best gen-6 findings, which improved along independent axes — the profit-leg measurement correction (fmb 4.76, alpha 4.5%) and the cyclically-purged decay penalty (alpha 4.2%, t 3.90) — so it is the single highest-value untested point for joint strength rather than a parameter variant. All legs are winsorized and unit-standardized, and the decay leg is a symmetric first difference rather than the zero-inflated drawdown product, so the composite should retain a strong cross-sectional slope.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( neg( ind_adj( delta( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Plus Research Intensity Less Rollover
input_signals.expression: SUB(ADD(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: If adding research spending back to operating profit works because expensing understates durable earning power, then unbundling the two — margin and research intensity as separate standardized channels — should be at least as informative and reveals whether the gain is a measurement correction or an independent intangible-intensity premium.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-6 jump from adding xrd into the numerator was large enough that its interpretation determines how the final signal should be built, and the constrained one-for-one add-back is only optimal if the two components deserve identical weights. Unbundling also lets research intensity contribute where margins are noisy, and comparing this against Signal 1 and the gen-6 leader identifies whether R&D belongs inside the profitability measure or beside it.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( add( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Less Innovation Funding Risk
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), RATIO(dlc, act)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A research-intensive firm facing near-term debt maturities out of thin liquid assets will cut the very spending that sustains its franchise, so refinancing pressure is far more damaging to durable profitability when the firm's earning power depends on a discretionary innovation program than when it does not.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a new interaction rather than a new leg: the fragility term is zero for non-innovators and grows only where funding pressure and research dependence co-occur, capturing an adjustment-cost channel (forced abandonment of intangible investment) that no balance-sheet or margin-decay measure represents. It also complements Signal 1 by asking whether R&D belongs in the *penalty* as a source of vulnerability as well as in the profit measure as understated strength.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( mul( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), ratio( dlc, act ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Plus Research Profit Less Rollover
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The cleanest measure of durable operating strength is the cash the business generates before discretionary innovation spending, since cash — not accrual profit — is what services maturing claims and funds the research program that sustains the franchise.
input_signals.reasoning: Profit-leg measurement is now the archive's most productive axis, and the one cash-based construct tested delivered the best Sharpe on record (0.44) before coverage limitations obscured it; pairing operating cash flow with the R&D add-back tests whether the accrual/cash distinction adds to the investment-measurement correction. Coverage will be lower because oancf begins later in the sample, so its statistics must be read alongside Signal 1 rather than on their own.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Industry Cumulative Earning Power Less Rollover
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 5), lt), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent earning power is best measured as five years of accumulated investment-adjusted operating profit relative to the current stock of creditor claims, judged against industry peers whose capital intensity and normal payback horizons differ.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-6 cumulative-flow version had the second-best FMB slope in the archive (3.84) despite lacking both the industry adjustment and the R&D correction that have since proven decisive, so applying both to it is the natural consolidation of the persistence channel. Comparing it with Signal 1 separates whether the payoff comes from a durable multi-year record of profit relative to obligations or from the current year's margin advantage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), 5 ), lt ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Intangible Capital Adjusted Profit Less Rollover
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: If research spending is an investment rather than an expense, then consistency requires treating it as investment on both sides of the profitability ratio: adding it back to operating profit *and* capitalizing the accumulated research stock into the capital base, so that innovators are neither penalized in the numerator nor flattered by an understated denominator.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the double-crediting error — R&D is added back only once, to a profit measure (oibdp) from which it genuinely was deducted — and replaces the published gross-profitability leg with an economically coherent return-on-invested-capital measure whose denominator includes five years of capitalized research. It is the natural completion of the gen-6 finding that drove the archive's best result (fmb 4.76, alpha 4.5%): if the correction belongs on both sides of the ratio, this should dominate the numerator-only version, and if it does not, the earlier gain was an intangible-intensity tilt rather than a measurement fix.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Full Sample Cash Innovation Profit Composite
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is the cash a business generates before discretionary research spending, measured relative to industry peers, discounted for near-term refinancing pressure and for firm-specific margin decay that the industry cycle does not explain.
input_signals.reasoning: This unites the archive's three strongest ingredients while repairing the cash leg's fatal coverage problem: where the cash-flow statement is unavailable in the early sample, funds from operations (income plus depreciation) is the standard economic substitute for operating cash flow, which is a justified missing-data convention rather than a coverage patch. If it retains the gen-7 cash signal's alpha (5.5%) and Sharpe (0.41) at roughly 0.11-0.12 coverage, it is the natural final consolidated signal.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( oancf, add( ib, dp ) ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( neg( ind_adj( delta( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Profit Less Rollover Less Funding Risk
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), RATIO(dlc, act)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Refinancing pressure damages all firms through forced asset sales and dilution, but damages research-intensive firms additionally by forcing abandonment of the intangible investment that sustains their franchise, so the innovation-specific vulnerability should be an extra penalty rather than a substitute for the general one.
input_signals.reasoning: The gen-7 version replaced the general rollover leg with the R&D-scaled interaction and lost alpha (2.3% versus 4.5%), which is exactly what the critic predicted would happen when the reliable penalty is discarded for the roughly half of firms with no research spending; supplementing instead of replacing tests whether the adjustment-cost mechanism has incremental content. The extra leg is identically zero for non-innovators, so it can only refine the ordering within the research-intensive part of the cross-section.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( mul( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), ratio( dlc, act ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Coherent Investment Adjusted Decay Composite
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: If research spending is investment rather than expense, then a firm that raises research spending is not experiencing margin decay, so the decay penalty must be computed on the same investment-adjusted profitability as the level leg.
input_signals.reasoning: The current leader mixes measurement conventions — an investment-adjusted level leg with a decay leg computed on unadjusted EBITDA — which mechanically penalizes firms that are stepping up research, exactly the firms the level leg rewards. Making the two legs internally consistent is a substantive economic correction, not a parameter tweak, and comparing it with the gen-7 leader tells us whether that inconsistency was helping (a genuine expense-discipline signal) or hurting (a measurement error).
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( neg( ind_adj( delta( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Profit Less Chronic Rollover Exposure
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_MAX(RATIO(dlc, act), 5), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes profitability fragile is chronic dependence on short-term funding across the cycle, not the level of maturing debt in one fiscal year, which is partly a timing accident of when the firm last termed out its borrowings.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has tested the current level, the maturity share, and the first difference of refinancing pressure, but never its worst realization over a full cycle, which is the state variable a creditor-run story implies should matter. Because the peak operator is monotone in a firm's funding policy rather than in its accounting timing, it should produce a more stable long-short composition and higher Sharpe if the chronic-exposure reading is correct, at a modest coverage cost from the five-year window.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ts_max( ratio( dlc, act ), 5 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Coverage Of Near Term Obligations
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(lct, xint)), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is best expressed as a coverage multiple — how many times the cash the business generates before discretionary research spending exceeds everything it must pay within the year, including all current liabilities and interest — because solvency is a ratio, not a difference, and its economic bite is nonlinear as the multiple approaches one.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a different functional form from the archive's entire standardized-difference family: the quality theme enters as the denominator so the signal compresses among safely covered firms and spreads sharply in the region where cash flow barely clears obligations, which is exactly where the profitability-durability distinction should bite. Industry z-scoring after winsorization makes the multiple comparable across sectors with structurally different payables cycles, and the denominator (current liabilities plus interest) is strictly positive for essentially every non-financial, so coverage is not sacrificed.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( oancf, add( ib, dp ) ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( lct, xint ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Profit With Funded Research Floor Less Rollover
input_signals.expression: SUB(ADD(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A franchise is durable when its research program has a funded floor — a level of research intensity the firm sustained even in its worst recent year — because opportunistic innovators cut research first when cash tightens, whereas committed innovators protect it and thereby protect future profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the near-binary reporting count with a continuous *intensity floor* (the five-year minimum of research spending per dollar of sales), which measures how much of the program survived the firm's own worst year rather than whether the firm files an R&D line, and it is industry-demeaned so it prices within-sector commitment rather than sector membership. The floor operator is the same downside-state logic that produced the archive's early gains on the profit side, now applied to the innovation channel that has proven to be the most powerful profitability ingredient.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( add( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ts_min( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 5 ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Innovation Profit Less Chronic Rollover Less Coherent Decay
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_MAX(RATIO(dlc, act), 5), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is industry-relative cash generation before discretionary research spending, discounted for a firm's worst refinancing exposure across the cycle and for idiosyncratic deterioration in that same cash-generating capability.
input_signals.reasoning: This assembles the three best-performing ingredients discovered — the cash-plus-research profit measure (best alpha and t-alpha), chronic rather than snapshot rollover exposure (best cross-sectional slope), and a decay leg measured on the same profitability definition as the level leg (best Sharpe) — into one internally consistent construct. Every adjustment has already been shown individually to raise at least one metric without harming the others, so this is the natural final consolidation candidate.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( coalesce( oancf, add( ib, dp ) ), coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ts_max( ratio( dlc, act ), 5 ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( neg( ind_adj( delta( ratio( add( oancf, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.reasoning: The intangible-capitalized denominator delivered a strong slope on its own (fmb 4.48) but has never been combined with the two legs that were subsequently shown to add alpha and Sharpe, so this candidate tests whether consistent capitalization on both sides of the profitability ratio survives inside the full composite. input_signals.name: Cash Innovation Profit Less Chronic Rollover
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_MAX(RATIO(dlc, act), 5), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The core economic interaction is simply industry-relative cash earning power before research spending set against the firm's chronic reliance on short-term funding; the decay penalty may be a refinement the two strongest legs no longer need.
input_signals.reasoning: The two ingredients here individually produced the archive's best alpha/t-alpha and best FMB slope respectively, and pairing them keeps coverage at roughly 0.12 rather than the 0.113 that the five-year decay leg costs. As the parsimonious member of the batch it is the correct benchmark for judging whether the extra legs in Signals 1-3 earn their complexity.

input_signals.name: Smoothed Innovation Profit Less Chronic Rollover Less Decay
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(TS_MAX(RATIO(dlc, act), 5), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Since the economic story is about durable rather than momentary earning power, the profitability leg should be a three-year average of investment-adjusted margin, which strips single-year windfalls and charges while leaving the decay leg to capture genuine deterioration.
input_signals.reasoning: Smoothing was tested only once, early, on a weak two-leg specification and never with the investment-adjusted profit measure that has since proven decisive; because the composite already contains an explicit decay leg, averaging the level leg cannot hide deterioration and should reduce turnover in the extreme portfolios. If Sharpe rises without a slope loss relative to Signal 2, the persistent-state reading of profitability is the right final refinement.

input_signals.name: Innovation Profit Less Net Funding Gap Less Coherent Decay
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dlc, SUB(act, lct)), at), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What threatens a profitable firm is the dollar amount of external funding it must actually raise next year — maturing debt in excess of the liquid working-capital slack available to repay it — so the economically correct penalty is a net funding shortfall scaled by assets, not a ratio of maturing debt to liquid assets.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a different economic object from every fragility leg tested: it nets liquidity against maturing claims into a single signed shortfall, so firms with surplus working capital score negative on the penalty (a genuine credit) while the ratio-based legs can only approach zero, and asset scaling makes it comparable across firms rather than fat-tailed like dlc/act. It requires no new data, keeps coverage at the full-sample level of the two-leg constructions, and pairs with the profit and coherent-decay legs that have already been shown to raise slope, alpha and Sharpe together.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( dlc, sub( act, lct ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( neg( ind_adj( delta( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Profit Less Unstable Short Funding Less Decay
input_signals.expression: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(dlc, act), 5), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm whose reliance on short-term debt swings from year to year lacks committed access to capital and is repeatedly at the mercy of funding markets, so instability of the funding structure — not merely its level or its worst reading — is what makes otherwise strong profitability fragile.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the algebraically degenerate peak-minus-current construction with a clean second-moment measure of funding policy, which is a dimension the archive has never tested on the liability side and which is not a monotone transform of either the snapshot or the peak exposure (a firm can be persistently high but stable, or low on average yet erratic). It uses the quality theme's preferred VOL operator on the archive's most productive fragility variable, and because the level of exposure is deliberately excluded, a strong result would identify capital-access instability rather than leverage as the mechanism.

input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), zscore( winsor( vol( ratio( dlc, act ), 5 ), 1 ) ) ), zscore( winsor( neg( ind_adj( delta( ratio( add( oibdp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )
